final_proof:
Fix p > 0 and recall that ℓ^p is the set of all real sequences x = (x_n)_{n∈ℕ} for which ∑_{n=1}^∞ |x_n|^p < ∞. (In the usual definition of the p-sequence spaces one assumes p ≥ 1; the argument below in fact also works when 0 < p < 1.) For x,y ∈ ℓ^p and a ∈ ℝ, define pointwise addition and scalar multiplication by (x+y)_n = x_n+y_n and (a·x)_n = ax_n. Here scalar multiplication is precisely pointwise multiplication of x by the constant sequence (a,a,…), viewed in the ambient ring of all real sequences.

We first prove that these operations are closed on ℓ^p. There is a constant C_p such that, for every u,v ≥ 0, (u+v)^p ≤ C_p(u^p+v^p): take C_p = 2^{p-1} when p ≥ 1, by convexity of t ↦ t^p, and C_p = 1 when 0 < p ≤ 1. For completeness, in the second case, if u+v > 0 and r=u/(u+v), then r^p ≥ r and (1-r)^p ≥ 1-r, so u^p+v^p ≥ (u+v)^p; the case u+v=0 is immediate. Hence, by the triangle inequality in ℝ,

∑_{n=1}^∞ |x_n+y_n|^p ≤ C_p ∑_{n=1}^∞ (|x_n|^p+|y_n|^p) < ∞.

Thus x+y ∈ ℓ^p. Also

∑_{n=1}^∞ |ax_n|^p = |a|^p ∑_{n=1}^∞ |x_n|^p < ∞,

where the equality and conclusion also hold when a=0. Therefore a·x ∈ ℓ^p. Thus both proposed operations are well-defined on the required domains.

It remains to verify the vector-space axioms. Let x=(x_n), y=(y_n), z=(z_n) ∈ ℓ^p and let a,b ∈ ℝ. Equality of sequences is coordinatewise, and in each coordinate the field laws in ℝ give

((x+y)+z)_n=(x_n+y_n)+z_n=x_n+(y_n+z_n)=(x+(y+z))_n,
(x+y)_n=x_n+y_n=y_n+x_n=(y+x)_n,
(a·(x+y))_n=a(x_n+y_n)=ax_n+ay_n=(a·x+a·y)_n,
((a+b)·x)_n=(a+b)x_n=ax_n+bx_n=(a·x+b·x)_n,
((ab)·x)_n=(ab)x_n=a(bx_n)=(a·(b·x))_n,
and (1·x)_n=x_n.

The zero sequence 0=(0,0,…) belongs to ℓ^p and satisfies (x+0)_n=x_n for every n. For every x ∈ ℓ^p, the sequence −x belongs to ℓ^p because ∑|−x_n|^p=∑|x_n|^p, and (x+(−x))_n=0 for every n. Consequently (ℓ^p,+) is an abelian group, scalar multiplication satisfies both distributive laws and the compatibility and identity laws, and all operations are closed. Therefore (ℓ^p,+,·) is a vector space over ℝ.
